texts: good. 'retreating' rides in the rule's condition, 'sometimes' sets the strength and is recorded as the quantifier word, and the tide-pools are kept as a group the rule can point at; only the plurality of 'small fish' flattens to one fish per tide, which costs nothing here.

bad: because 'the trapped fish' is definite, the translator minted a separate fish for every keeper inside the rule and left the fish's existence out of the knowledge base entirely, so nothing can be asked about the trapped fish afterwards. Drop the article so the object is an ordinary kind: 'Keepers take trapped fish home on harvest mornings.' If the tide-pool link matters, spell it out instead: 'Keepers take fish trapped in the tide-pools home on harvest mornings.'
good. the ebb is one typed individual carrying 'slow' and 'underwater', the harbor mouth is recorded as part of the harbor, and the ebb is located in it.

good. 'out of the harbor' becomes the source of the running, the ebb correctly undergoes the motion rather than driving it, and 'at low tide' is kept as a plain time constant. (Worth knowing: 'the deep ebb' fuses into a deep-ebb kind here where the previous sentence typed it as an ebb that is deep -- both still answer to 'ebb', so nothing is lost.)

mixed: the bitterness and the 'slightly' both survive, but 'tastes' has no carrier at all, so the parse records the water AS slightly bitter rather than as tasting so -- the sensory modality is silently gone. If the taste itself matters, make it a noun: 'The water of the deep ebb has a slightly bitter taste.'
good. the Warden is typed as a warden, Cauldron Hall is kept as a name with its own kind atom, and the two are joined by the loose-association link that a name-premodified title licenses.
